skill.name: wiki-vitepress
skill.description: Packages generated wiki Markdown into a VitePress static site with dark theme, Mermaid diagram styling, click-to-zoom diagrams, and production build output.
skill.summary: Packages generated wiki Markdown into a dark VitePress static site with Mermaid diagram support.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and reconnaissance alerts are markdown backtick, CSS, or documentation false positives rather than executable Ruby or reconnaissance behavior. One real client-side issue remains: the Mermaid zoom modal copies element HTML into innerHTML, and the documented npm build command executes dependencies and project scripts.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the innerHTML assignment with cloneNode(true), or sanitize generated HTML before inserting it into the modal.
Document expected packages, commit a lockfile, and prefer npm ci before running the VitePress build.
State that build commands should run only inside the generated wiki-site directory after user approval.

static_findings.snippet: Generate the following structure in a `wiki-site/` directory:
- Configure `themeConfig.nav` and `themeConfig.sidebar` from the catalogue structure
Mermaid inline `style` attributes override everything. Use `onMounted` + polling to replace them:
Use `setup()` with `onMounted`, NOT `enhanceApp()` — DOM doesn't exist during SSR.
Wrap each `.mermaid` container in a clickable wrapper that opens a fullscreen modal:
Before VitePress build, scan all `.md` files and fix:
- Wrap bare `<T>` generic parameters in backticks outside code fences
- Ensure every page has YAML frontmatter with `title` and `description`
- Mermaid renders async — SVGs don't exist when `onMounted` fires. Must poll.
- `isCustomElement` compiler option for bare `<T>` causes worse crashes — do NOT use it
- Node text in Mermaid uses inline `style` with highest specificity — CSS alone won't fix it
- `enhanceApp()` runs during SSR where `document` doesn't exist — use `setup()` only

content.value_statement: Generated wiki pages are hard to browse as loose Markdown files. This skill packages them into a dark VitePress site with Mermaid diagram support.
actual_capabilities: Creates a wiki-site directory structure for VitePress.
Defines config requirements for VitePress and vitepress-plugin-mermaid.
Specifies dark Mermaid theme variables and CSS overrides.
Adds client-side Mermaid style polling and click-to-zoom modal guidance.
Lists Markdown cleanup rules before build.
limitations: Assumes Node.js, npm, VitePress, and vitepress-plugin-mermaid are available.
Does not generate the wiki Markdown content itself.
Requires review before using generated innerHTML modal code with untrusted content.
May need manual sidebar and nav adjustments for unusual wiki structures.

use_cases.title: Publish Engineering Wiki
use_cases.description: Turn generated project documentation into a static site that developers can browse locally or deploy.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Diagrams
use_cases.description: Build a site where Mermaid diagrams use dark styling and open in a fullscreen view.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Documentation
use_cases.description: Package Markdown pages into production build output for release notes or internal docs.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-vitepress and configure dark Mermaid styling for every diagram in the generated wiki.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Production Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-vitepress to create the site, apply Markdown cleanup rules, and build production output.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Navigation and Diagram UX
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wiki-vitepress to generate nav, sidebar, dark Mermaid styling, and click-to-zoom behavior for a multi-section wiki.

output_examples.input: Package these generated wiki pages into a VitePress site.
output: Created the wiki-site structure with pages and theme files.
Configured dark VitePress styling and Mermaid support.
Prepared build output guidance for the VitePress dist folder.

output_examples.input: Make Mermaid diagrams readable in dark mode.
output_examples.output: The generated theme uses Mermaid dark variables, CSS overrides, and client-side style replacement for rendered SVG text.
The result is a VitePress project that can install dependencies and produce static files in the VitePress dist folder.

best_practices: Review generated Markdown for Vue template conflicts before building.
Keep Mermaid content trusted or sanitize diagram HTML before enabling the zoom modal.
Run dependency installation in a controlled project directory.
anti_patterns: Do not run the build in a repository root without checking generated file paths.
Do not use the innerHTML zoom pattern with untrusted Markdown content.
Do not skip frontmatter generation for pages that need navigation metadata.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a VitePress site scaffold for generated wiki Markdown. It also defines dark Mermaid diagram behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate the wiki content?
faq.answer: No. It packages existing generated Markdown pages into a browsable static site.

faq.question: Does it support Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It specifies dark theme variables, CSS overrides, and click-to-zoom behavior for Mermaid diagrams.

faq.question: What build output is expected?
faq.answer: The documented output path is wiki-site/.vitepress/dist after the VitePress build finishes.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow expects Node.js, npm, VitePress, and vitepress-plugin-mermaid.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted Markdown?
faq.answer: Use caution. The suggested zoom modal uses innerHTML, so untrusted content should be sanitized or avoided.
